With ONE file they still fail. So neither can go green on an empty set. r5-reconciliation.title: Reconciliation check
r5-reconciliation.imperative: Does the change diverge from the recorded architecture in a way Commander must reconcile? Record pass/fail; flag a triage candidate if it is out of scope.
r5-reconciliation.finding: Map Impact notes check out against the diff and the evidence, with one correction. VERIFIED: constraint:engine-runs-command-checks-with-no-cwd holds exactly as stated -- _run_check_command at :881-883 calls subprocess.run([shell,'-c',command]) with no cwd, and _check_condition's base_dir really is used only by the git-change-policy branch, so it is not a latent way out. constraint:shipped-content-must-not-carry-machine-specific-absolute-paths is now an executable guard I observed failing on pre-fix content and on 6 fresh mutants. decision:demo-spine-is-generated-not-hand-fixed resolved to candidate (b) on a reason I reproduced (test_mcp_spine_server.py:588 json-loads .mcp.json's SPINE_FILE default, which is this spine), so the regrade from guess to measured is earned. claim:605-demo-unusable is discharged -- I drove it to DONE twice with negative controls. CORRECTION to the implementer's note: it says the engine runs checks under a POSIX shell and the new test proves expansion under 'bash', but _find_posix_shell returns shutil.which('sh') on POSIX and only prefers bash on Windows -- on this host the engine used /usr/bin/sh (dash). I re-verified the nested ${A:-${B:-c}}/$(id -u) expansion under dash directly and it is identical, so the design is correct on both; the test's shell is a fidelity gap, not a defect. No divergence from recorded architecture that Commander must reconcile. Triage candidates recorded separately.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to .agent-work/cleanup-a-door/FOWLER_PASS.json (from templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/cleanup-a-door/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command resolves the record path from cleanup-a-door alone -- the same substitution you already make everywhere else in this survey (line 2) -- so no separate placeholder to fill and no way to leave it stale. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record path ever needs to move off that fixed convention, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

triage_candidates.statement: No test exercises the demo spine's DEFAULT workspace branch. Both ShippedDemoDrivesFromAnyDirectoryTests methods set SPINE_DEMO_WORKSPACE (tests/test_shipped_examples_are_portable.py:309), so the committed default ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/constellation-mcp-demo-$(id -u) is only asserted for absoluteness, never driven. I drove it end to end by hand from $HOME and it works, so this is a coverage gap, not a defect. Cheapest fix: one more drive case with SPINE_DEMO_WORKSPACE unset, pointed at a TMPDIR the test controls.

tests/test_shipped_examples_are_portable.py:289 expands the check path with 'bash -c', but checklist_engine._find_posix_shell returns shutil.which('sh') on POSIX and prefers bash only on Windows -- so on Linux the test asserts under a shell the engine never uses (here: /usr/bin/sh, dash). I verified dash expands the nested ${A:-${B:-c}} and $(id -u) identically, so nothing is broken today; the test would just miss a future bashism. Cheapest fix: call checklist_engine._find_posix_shell() instead of hardcoding bash.
